headline_marked: 2,000 accused in 4 cases after [[Mirpur hawker eviction clash]]
headline: 2,000 accused in 4 cases after Mirpur hawker eviction clash
summary: Police and DNCC officials have filed cases following violent clashes during an eviction drive at Mirpur-10 roundabout, resulting in 25 arrests.
details: Four separate cases have been filed following violent clashes, arson, and vandalism during an illegal structure eviction drive at the Mirpur-10 roundabout area in Dhaka.
Two of the cases were filed by the police at Mirpur Model Police Station, while the other two were filed by Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) officials at Mirpur Model and Kafrul police stations.
Police stated that a total of 2,000 people have been accused across the four cases, with 20 individuals specifically named in the FIRs. So far, 25 people have been arrested.
During the clash between hawkers, police, and DNCC workers, three DNCC vehicles were set on fire and one police vehicle was vandalized. Several police officers and journalists were also attacked.

The cases filed by the police allege attacks on force members, causing injuries, obstructing government duties, and vandalizing vehicles and traffic boxes. The DNCC cases focus on the arson of their vehicles.
According to Mirpur Model Police Station OC Hafizur Rahman, 30 people were initially detained, and after verification, 25 were arrested while five were released.
Kafrul Police Station OC Mohammad Saiful Islam noted that a case regarding the burning of vehicles has been filed by a DNCC official, though no arrests have been made in that specific case yet.

headline_marked: US provides [[500,000 dengue test kits]] to Bangladesh
headline: US provides 500,000 dengue test kits to Bangladesh
summary: The kits will be distributed to district and upazila hospitals across the country to strengthen dengue diagnosis.
details: The United States has provided 500,000 dengue test kits to Bangladesh to assist in the fight against the virus.
Health Minister Sardar Mohammad Sakhavat Hossain announced this during a handover ceremony at Kurmitola Hospital in Dhaka on Thursday morning.
The provided kits are NS1 rapid diagnostic kits, which allow for quick detection of the dengue virus.
Health Minister Hossain stated that these kits will be distributed to upazila and district hospitals across the country in phases.
He further mentioned that the government currently has an adequate stock of dengue test kits and remains fully prepared to handle the situation.
